brief.headline: Push for 8–12% price cut — they keep 8.5% profit vs peer 4.8%, so there's room; offer 30-day payment in exchange.

priceAsk.summary: Ask for an 8–12% price reduction on rigid plastic packaging
priceAsk.target: ₹2.10–3.14 L annual saving (8–12% of ₹26.17 L spend)
priceAsk.basis: They keep 8.5% profit vs 4.8% for similar firms — nearly double. That cushion belongs in our price. Market ask for 28 mm caps runs ₹0.55–1.20/pc, typical ₹0.85–0.95/pc; verdict is MARKET-FAIR with modest headroom to ₹0.65–0.80 at higher volume. Our target sits in that range.

paymentTermAsk.summary: Offer to move from 45 days to 30 days, in exchange for the price cut
paymentTermAsk.cashImpact: Costs us ₹2.15 L in cash (we pay 15 days earlier), but we get back ₹2.10–3.14 L in annual savings — a net win of about ₹1 L or more per year

brief.financialLeverage: Triveni is healthy — zero debt (0.00x), strong interest cover (75.84x), safe zone (Altman 6.18) — so they won't break. But we're tiny: ₹26.17 L is just 0.15% of their ₹179.69 Cr revenue, so alone we have little pull. Their cash is stuck for 124 days (vs peer 114 days), meaning cash is a bit tighter than similar firms. They also have an EPF payment delay flag. Use the payment-term swap (30 days frees them ₹2.15 L of our cash faster) as the carrot, and line up Manjushree Technopack (₹2569.83 Cr, B-rated, India's largest rigid-plastic converter) or Mold-Tek as a credible second source to show we can walk.

evidence.point: They keep 8.5% profit, nearly double the 4.8% peer median — room in their price
We're a tiny customer — ₹26.17 L is 0.15% of their ₹179.69 Cr revenue
Their cash is stuck for 124 days, longer than peer 114 days — so faster payment has value to them
Zero debt and strong cover (75.84x) — financially safe, not fragile
Market ask for 28 mm PP cap is ₹0.55–1.20/pc, typical ₹0.85–0.95/pc, with headroom to ₹0.65–0.80 at volume
evidence.figure: marketAsk: ₹0.55–1.20/pc, typical ₹0.85–0.95/pc, verdict MARKET-FAIR; headroom to ₹0.65–0.80

evidence.point: EPF payment delays flagged — a minor compliance issue that signals some operational tightness

alternates.name: Manjushree Technopack Ltd
alternates.why: India's largest rigid-plastic packaging converter (₹2569.83 Cr revenue, B 65/100 health) — pharma bottles, caps, preforms; top second-source candidate for our packaging

alternates.name: Mold-Tek Packaging Ltd
alternates.why: Listed rigid-plastic leader (pails, containers, pharma) — strong, profitable, robust alternate for bottles and closures

alternates.name: Reliance Industries Limited
alternates.role: a lead to qualify (verify before RFQ) — India-Pan manufacturer, medium confidence; potential resin/preform source

risks: We're only 0.15% of their business — on our own we have little leverage; bundle more SKUs or commit longer term to gain weight
Their cash cycle is 124 days (peer 114 days) and they have an EPF delay — pushing too hard on both price and payment could strain them; lead with the payment swap as a give, not a take
Market ask verdict is MARKET-FAIR — our current price may already be reasonable; the ask hinges on their profit cushion (8.5% vs 4.8%), not on us overpaying today
Alternates like Manjushree and Mold-Tek are much larger — qualifying and switching will take time; use them as negotiating leverage now, but have a fallback plan if Triveni won't move
brief.suggestedOpeningLine: We'd like to work with you long-term, but at ₹26.17 L your pricing needs to reflect the 8.5% profit margin you're keeping — nearly double your peers at 4.8% — so we're here to close that gap and offer faster payment in return.
